broker.spoolRetryAllWarning: Every failed and dead-letter entry is put back into the queue. They are delivered as soon as the target answers again.

broker.spoolNone: Nothing queued — every instance reached its target.
broker.spoolDiscardHint: The spooled instance is deleted — it will never reach the PACS. This cannot be undone; the reason is recorded in the change log.

broker.stationSubtitle: Per-station worklist filter and source priority
broker.stationHint: A rule applies to the ScheduledStationAETitle of the query. 'deny' hides the listed sources from that console, 'allow' shows only them. The filter runs after the merge, so deduplication stays the same for every station.
broker.stationDialogHint: The station AE title must match the value the console sends; '*' is the fallback for every station without its own rule.
broker.stationAetHint: '*' applies to every station that has no exact rule.
broker.stationPreviewHint: Which sources would this console see, and in which order do they win the dedupe?
broker.atnaHint: IHE audit messages (DICOM PS3.15) as syslog to your own Audit Record Repository. Delivery never blocks DICOM traffic; a full buffer drops messages and is counted.

broker.atnaProtocolHint: 6514 is the usual syslog-over-TLS port, 514 plain syslog.
broker.atnaTestOk: The repository accepted the test message.
broker.tlsHint: Encrypted DICOM for the modalities and/or RIS/PACS. Off by default — a LAN/VPN setup keeps working unchanged, and plain and TLS can run side by side.
broker.tlsInboundHint: A second listener next to the plain port: move one modality at a time.
broker.tlsClientAuthHint: mTLS needs a CA file that signed the modality certificates.
broker.tlsOutboundVerifyHint: Leave it on. Switch it off only for a self-signed lab system — the connection is then encrypted but the peer is not authenticated.
broker.tlsOutboundHint: These files apply to every outgoing connection that has TLS switched on (per source/target).
broker.tlsGenerateHint: For installations without their own PKI: generate the certificate here, hand the public part to the modality or PACS vendor, then switch TLS on. The private key stays in the broker.
broker.tlsGenerateCnHint: The name the other side will see — usually the broker's host name.
broker.tlsGenerateSanHint: IP addresses and host names the certificate is valid for. Without an entry the common name is used.
broker.tlsGenerateCaHint: Generates a CA certificate — useful when several devices should trust the broker.
broker.tlsGenerateHandOver: Hand this public certificate to the other side (or import it as trusted there).
broker.tlsTestHint: Performs a real TLS handshake and shows protocol, cipher and the peer certificate. With an AE title it also runs a C-ECHO over TLS — the check before a modality or PACS is switched over.
broker.tlsEnabledHint: Off = the plain LAN/VPN connection (the default).
broker.tlsVerifyHint: Recommended. Off only for a self-signed lab system.
broker.tlsVerifyWarning: Verification is off: the connection is encrypted, but the peer is not authenticated.
broker.health_tls_verification_disabled: Outgoing connections are encrypted but the remote certificate is not verified.
broker.health_tls_configuration_incomplete: The TLS listener is enabled but its certificate or key is missing.
broker.health_tls_file_unusable: A configured TLS file cannot be used: {{path}}
broker.health_tls_key_mismatch: A private key does not belong to its certificate.
broker.health_tls_key_world_readable: A private key is readable by other users ({{mode}}).

broker.localStudyUidHint: Optional; the modality gets the UID back if it is known.
broker.targetDefaultWarning: This is the default target: without a routing rule, incoming images have no destination afterwards.
broker.discardHint: The form contains changes that have not been saved yet.
broker.duplicateAet: This AE title is already used by {{name}} — two nodes with the same AE title cannot be told apart.

broker.tagInvalid: DICOM tag or keyword expected, e.g. (0010,0010) or PatientName.
broker.i18nBrokerNote: The visible interface is translated; the detailed help texts are available in German and English (English fills the rest).
broker.errHost: Enter the address only: no spaces, no slashes, no http://.
broker.helpIntro: Short version: what the page is for, what to fill in and what usually goes wrong.
help_sources_what: The broker does not keep the worklist itself — it asks your RIS/KIS systems and passes the answers to the modality.
Every system you ask is one source here. The modality only talks to the broker.
help_sources_how: Name: any label you recognise (e.g. "ris-main"). It only appears in this UI and in the logs.
AE title: the name the RIS expects — upper case, 1–16 characters, only A–Z 0–9 _ -.
Host and port: address and DICOM port of the RIS. Ask your RIS vendor if you are unsure.
Priority: lower number = asked first. With two sources knowing the same order, the lower one wins.
help_sources_wrong: The address typed as a sentence ("ris server 1") or with http:// — only the address belongs here.
A lower-case AE title: DICOM expects upper case (the field corrects it automatically).
The same AE title twice — two systems with the same name cannot be told apart (you get a warning while typing).
After saving, use the C-ECHO button in the list: it proves the broker really reaches the system.
help_targets_what: Images the modality sends to the broker are forwarded to a PACS.
A target is one PACS. Exactly one should be marked as the default.
help_targets_how: AE title, host and port of the PACS — the same three values as in the PACS configuration.
Default: yes for the PACS that should receive everything without a special rule.
help_targets_wrong: Deleting the default target: afterwards images without a routing rule have no destination at all.
Two defaults: which one wins is then a matter of luck — keep exactly one.
No C-ECHO test after changing the address: images are then quietly spooled instead of arriving.
help_rules_what: A rule decides which PACS receives images from which source (e.g. everything from the emergency RIS goes to the emergency PACS).
Without a matching rule, images go to the default target.
help_rules_how: Source: where the images come from (including the pseudo source "local" for emergencies).
Target: which PACS should receive them.
Priority: if several rules match, the lowest number wins.
help_rules_wrong: Two rules for the same source and target — that is ambiguous and blocked here.
A rule that was meant for a single device but applies to the whole source: check the preview on the station page.
Testing only in production: create the rule, send one image, then check the store log.
help_transforms_what: Before forwarding, the broker can change individual DICOM fields — e.g. add the institution name or shorten an accession number.
This is only cosmetic metadata; the image itself is never changed.
help_transforms_how: Name: what the rule is for (e.g. "set institution name").
Tag: either a keyword (PatientName) or the number in the form (0010,0010).
Operation: set, remove, prefix, suffix, replace or copy from another tag.
help_transforms_wrong: A tag that does not exist — the field says so immediately.
Changing a UID: the broker refuses this, it would break the link to the images.
Forgetting to test: use the simulation on the overview page before letting real images through.
help_stations_what: Every console should only see its own worklist. A station rule decides which sources a console may see.
The rule matches the station AE title the modality sends.
help_stations_how: Station AE title: exactly as configured in the modality (or * for all stations).
Mode: "deny" hides the listed sources, "allow" shows only the listed ones.
Priority: controls the order in which sources are merged for this console.
help_stations_wrong: Mode "allow" without a source: that console then sees an empty worklist (you get a warning).
A typo in the AE title: the rule simply never matches — check the exact spelling in the modality.
Use the preview button: it shows what this console would receive right now.
help_worklist_what: Emergencies and unscheduled examinations exist in no RIS. The broker keeps them here and mixes them into every worklist answer.
Orders can also arrive automatically as HL7 messages (from the RIS or an admission system).
help_worklist_how: Accession number: required — this is what the modality searches for.
Patient name in DICOM form: Last^First (e.g. Mueller^Hans).
Date and time: use the pickers; the entry only matches the day you set here.
Leave the station empty to make the entry visible for every console.
help_worklist_wrong: A date typed by hand instead of using the picker — then the entry never shows up on that day.
A missing accession number: the modality cannot find the entry.
Forgetting the expiry: without a validity date the entry stays until it is deleted.
help_spool_what: If a PACS is unreachable, the broker keeps the images and sends them later — nothing is lost.
This page shows what is waiting, what is being retried and what could not be delivered.
help_spool_how: Filter by status to see only what needs attention ("dead" = delivery failed repeatedly).
Retry sends an entry again — use it after the PACS is reachable.
Discard removes an entry permanently; a reason is required and is written to the audit log.
help_spool_wrong: Discarding instead of retrying: the image is then gone from the queue.
A full spool means the PACS has been unreachable for a long time — check the health panel first.
help_audit_what: Every configuration change is recorded here with time, user and the changed values.
This is the trace for "who changed what, and when?" — and the way back if a change went wrong.
help_audit_how: Open an entry to see the difference before/after.
Roll back restores the state from before that change.
Export/import moves a whole configuration between installations (import always shows a preview first).
help_audit_wrong: Rolling back a change that later changes depend on — check the current state afterwards.
Importing a configuration without reading the preview: it overwrites matching entries.
help_settings_what: The runtime settings of the broker: timeouts, worklist cache, C-STORE spool, circuit breaker, HL7 intake, retention, audit trail (ATNA), alerting and DICOM TLS.
Below the list sit the cards for the things that need more than one value: alerting (webhook and events), retention, TLS certificates and the audit trail.
Nothing here is a one-way street: every value shows where it comes from, and 'reset' brings back the value the installation was built with.
help_settings_how: Each row shows the current value and where it comes from (".env" = deployment default, "override" = changed here).
Save applies the value immediately; "reset" returns to the deployment default.
Numbers show their allowed range underneath.
help_settings_wrong: A value outside the range: the field says so and blocks saving.
Forgetting that a change applies immediately — the echo interval, cache and spool react at once.
help_overview_what: The broker sits between the modalities and your RIS/PACS: it collects the worklists and forwards the images.
This page shows at a glance whether everything is reachable and whether anything is waiting.
help_overview_how: Green "ok" next to a source or target means the C-ECHO test just succeeded.
The cards below show what needs attention: unreachable systems, waiting images, cached worklists.
Use the sidebar to configure: sources (RIS), targets (PACS), rules, station rules, settings.
help_overview_wrong: Red or grey entries are the first thing to look at — a console with an empty worklist usually means an unreachable source.
"Spool" entries that keep growing mean the PACS cannot be reached.
If something was misconfigured, the change log on the audit page has the way back.
broker.setting_upstream_timeout_s: Timeout for one upstream C-FIND query (s)
broker.setting_audit_actor_header: Header that carries the operator identity
broker.setting_breaker_fail_threshold: Failures before a source is skipped
broker.setting_breaker_open_seconds: Cooldown of an open circuit breaker (s)
broker.settingDesc_allowed_calling_aets: Comma-separated calling AE titles allowed to query/store (empty = allow all).
broker.settingDesc_strict_store_status: Report a DIMSE failure to the modality when forwarding fails.
broker.settingDesc_seen_item_ttl_days: Days that seen_items rows are kept for store routing (retention purge).
broker.settingDesc_echo_interval_s: Interval of the C-ECHO monitoring loop in seconds.
broker.settingDesc_upstream_timeout_s: Timeout for one upstream C-FIND query in seconds.
broker.settingDesc_audit_actor_header: Header that carries the operator identity (empty = 'api').
broker.settingDesc_rbac_mode: enforce: configuration writes need the write role in the roles header.
broker.settingDesc_rbac_roles_header: Header the proxy uses to pass the user's roles (comma separated).
broker.settingDesc_rbac_write_role: Role that allows changing the configuration (brokerWrite).
broker.settingDesc_retention_query_log_days: Keep worklist query logs for this many days (0 = forever).
broker.settingDesc_retention_store_log_days: Retention of the forwarded-instance log in days (0 = keep forever).
broker.settingDesc_retention_local_items_days: Also delete local worklist items older than this (0 = only their own validity applies).
broker.settingDesc_retention_hl7_days: Keep inbound HL7 messages for this many days (0 = forever).
broker.settingDesc_retention_spool_days: Keep spool entries (delivered and dead letters) for this many days (0 = forever).
broker.settingDesc_retention_config_audit_days: Keep the configuration change log for this many days (0 = forever, recommended).
broker.settingDesc_tls_inbound_enabled: Offer a TLS listener for the modalities (next to the plain port).
broker.settingDesc_tls_inbound_port: Port of the TLS listener (2762 is the usual DICOM TLS port).
broker.settingDesc_tls_inbound_key_file: Private key of the server certificate (PEM, unencrypted).
broker.settingDesc_tls_inbound_ca_file: CA bundle used to verify modality certificates (for mTLS).
broker.settingDesc_tls_inbound_client_auth: Whether modalities must present a certificate (mTLS).
broker.settingDesc_tls_outbound_ca_file: CA bundle used to verify RIS/PACS certificates (empty = system store).
broker.settingDesc_tls_outbound_client_cert_fil: Certificate the broker presents to RIS/PACS (for mTLS).
broker.settingDesc_tls_outbound_client_key_file: Private key of that certificate (PEM, unencrypted).
broker.settingDesc_tls_outbound_verify: Verify the remote certificate on outgoing connections.
broker.settingDesc_tls_dir: Directory for certificates the broker generates itself.
broker.settingDesc_local_priority: Merge priority of local worklist items (lower wins; default before every source).
broker.settingDesc_local_default_validity_days: Default validity of a manually created local item in days (0 = unlimited).
broker.settingDesc_hl7_enabled: Accept HL7 ORM orders over the REST endpoint.
broker.settingDesc_hl7_mllp_enabled: Listen for HL7 ORM messages on the MLLP port as well.
broker.settingDesc_hl7_mllp_bind: Interface the MLLP listener binds to.
broker.settingDesc_hl7_mllp_port: MLLP port the RIS sends ORM messages to.
broker.settingDesc_hl7_default_station_aet: Scheduled station used when an ORM message carries no station AE title.
broker.settingDesc_hl7_default_modality: Modality used when an ORM message carries none.
broker.settingDesc_atna_enabled: Send IHE ATNA audit messages to an Audit Record Repository.
broker.settingDesc_atna_syslog_host: Host of the audit repository (syslog/TLS receiver).
broker.settingDesc_atna_syslog_port: Port of the audit repository (6514 = syslog over TLS, 514 = plain).
broker.settingDesc_atna_tls_ca_file: Optional CA bundle used to verify the audit repository (TLS only).
broker.settingDesc_atna_queue_max: Maximum buffered audit messages before the oldest are dropped.
broker.settingDesc_notify_webhook_url: Webhook that receives broker alerts (Slack/Teams-compatible JSON, comma separated for several targets, empty = off).
broker.settingDesc_notify_events: Comma-separated event codes to send (see GET /notify/events).
broker.settingDesc_notify_min_interval_s: Minimum distance between two messages for the same event and object.
broker.settingDesc_spool_enabled: Spool C-STORE instances that cannot be forwarded and retry them later.
broker.settingDesc_accept_when_queued: Report success to the modality once the instance is safely spooled.
broker.settingDesc_spool_dir: Directory the spooled DICOM files are written to (own volume recommended).
broker.settingDesc_spool_max_items: Maximum number of spooled instances before the spool refuses new ones.
broker.settingDesc_spool_max_bytes: Maximum spool size in bytes before it refuses new instances.
broker.settingDesc_spool_max_attempts: Forwarding attempts before an instance becomes a dead letter.
broker.settingDesc_spool_backoff_s: Base delay of the exponential retry backoff in seconds.
broker.settingDesc_spool_retention_s: How long a forwarded entry stays as a duplicate guard (seconds).
broker.settingDesc_spool_poll_s: Interval of the spool retry worker in seconds.
broker.settingDesc_cache_enabled: Serve cached worklist answers when an upstream source is unreachable.
broker.settingDesc_cache_stale_max_s: Hard cap for serving cached answers after the last successful query (0 = never).
broker.settingDesc_cache_hide_completed: Never return COMPLETED/DISCONTINUED steps from the cache.
broker.settingDesc_cache_max_items: Maximum number of worklist items cached per source.
broker.settingDesc_breaker_fail_threshold: Consecutive C-FIND failures per source before its circuit breaker opens.
broker.settingDesc_breaker_open_seconds: How long an open breaker stays open before the next attempt.
broker.settingDesc_retention_mpps_days: How long performed procedure steps (MPPS) are kept — 0 = forever.
broker.settingDesc_spool_lease_s: How long one instance may hold a claimed spool entry before another may take it over. Must be longer than the store timeout of the targets.
broker.settingDesc_instance_id: Name of this broker instance. Set it when several instances share one database (high availability) — otherwise the host name and process ID are used.
broker.settingDesc_ha_heartbeat_s: How often this instance reports that it is alive.
broker.settingDesc_ha_instance_timeout_s: An instance counts as gone when it has not reported for this long — three heartbeats is a good value.
broker.settingDesc_mpps_enabled: Accept MPPS from the modalities. Without it the RIS never learns that an examination was performed.
broker.setting_mpps_forward_enabled: Report the state to the RIS
broker.settingDesc_mpps_forward_enabled: Report the MPPS state back to the RIS as an HL7 message.
broker.settingDesc_mpps_forward_host: Host of the RIS that receives the state messages.
broker.settingDesc_mpps_forward_url: Webhook URL for the state message when the transport is 'webhook'.
broker.settingDesc_mpps_forward_facility: Receiving facility of the RIS in the status message. Some HL7 engines reject a message without it.
broker.settingDesc_mpps_hide_completed: Hide completed steps from the worklist the broker serves.
broker.settingDesc_hl7_store_raw: Keep the raw HL7 message for troubleshooting and replay. The message contains patient data (PHI) — off by default.
broker.setting_simulate_show_phi: Show patient data in the preview
broker.settingDesc_simulate_show_phi: Include patient name and ID in the worklist preview (off = PHI-free, like the query log).
broker.eventDesc_breaker_open: A source was skipped after repeated C-FIND failures.
broker.eventDesc_config_error: The configuration health checks found an error.
broker.eventDesc_source_down: An upstream worklist source stopped answering C-ECHO.
broker.eventDesc_spool_backlog: Instances are waiting in the spool for too long.
broker.eventDesc_spool_dead_letter: A spooled instance gave up and needs attention.
broker.eventDesc_spool_full: The C-STORE spool is full — new instances are refused.
broker.eventDesc_target_down: A PACS target stopped answering C-ECHO.
broker.eventDesc_tls_certificate_expiring: A configured TLS certificate expires soon.
broker.sinceHint: Only entries from this day on. Empty = all.
broker.previewHint: Runs the real C-FIND aggregation (all sources, merge, station rule, cache) — nothing is stored for routing.
broker.previewEmpty: No answers — check the sources and the station rule.
broker.previewTruncated: More entries exist than are shown.
broker.queryTestHint: Asks this source directly whether it delivers worklists — a C-ECHO only says it is alive.
broker.hl7DetailHint: What was parsed, what the broker did with it and why it failed.
broker.hl7NotReplayable: The raw message was not stored (setting hl7_store_raw) — the sender has to resend it.
broker.tlsUploadTitle: Install a certificate from the PKI
broker.tlsUploadHint: Certificate and key are checked (the key must belong to it and it must be valid). The key is stored with mode 0600 and never shown again.
broker.mppsHint: What the modalities reported and whether it reached the RIS. Finished steps are removed from the worklist.
broker.mppsForwardOff: Reporting to the RIS is switched off.
broker.mppsHideCompleted: Finished steps are hidden from the worklist.
broker.mppsRetryOneHint: Delivers this step's state to the RIS again.
broker.mergeHint: Normally the whole entry comes from the highest-priority source. Here you can decide per attribute which source wins — e.g. patient data from the HIS feed, the study description from the RIS.
broker.mergeSourcesHint: First source that has a value wins. Everything else still comes from the winning entry.
broker.hl7MapHint: Some systems send the room or the contrast agent in a field of their own. Map it to a worklist attribute here — no code change for a local convention.
broker.hl7MapEmpty: No extra mappings — only the standard fields are read.
broker.hl7MapComponentHint: Component counts like HL7 does (OBR-18.2 → component 2; 0 = the whole field). The dry run shows what a mapping filled.
broker.matrixHint: Compares several stations at once — the check before a rollout. Empty = every station with a rule.
broker.matrixWarning: At least one console would see an empty worklist.
broker.pirHint: An old patient ID now belongs to the current one. A merge (ADT A40) retires the old ID — the worklist answer follows it; a link (A24) only records that both records are the same person, both IDs stay valid.
broker.pirSameId: Old and current ID are the same — nothing to do.
broker.pirSavedMerge: Merge recorded: {{items}} worklist entries and {{provenance}} routing rows now use the current ID.
broker.pirSavedLink: Link recorded — both IDs stay valid, nothing was moved.
broker.mergeEmpty: No field rules — the normal merge applies.
broker.pirProbeHint: ID as the modality sends it
broker.pirEffectMerge: A merge retires the old ID: the worklist answer and the routing follow the current one.
broker.pirEffectLink: A link keeps both IDs valid: nothing is moved and no answer is rewritten.

about.description: Modern React/TypeScript frontend for the Orthanc DICOM server — standalone SPA (Docker sidecar, Orthanc plugin or behind a JWT-authenticated backend proxy) with audited writes and a configuration a deployment can preset and lock. Study management, merge/migrate, smart search, upload, modality and DICOMweb configuration, viewer integration incl. the IHE image display entry point (RAD-106). It also ships the MWL broker: a DICOM Modality Worklist proxy that fans out to several RIS/KIS systems, merges and caches their worklists, serves the modalities, reports MPPS back to the RIS, accepts HL7 orders (ORM/OMG/OMI) and ADT patient updates (incl. PIR), and routes the stored images to the right PACS — with store spool, per-source cache, store log, TLS/mTLS, ATNA and retention. Verified against DCMTK, dcm4che and DVTk.
